title: Is the Rise in Cohabitation Fueling a Marriage Slowdown?
gist: Delano Squires argues that cohabitation before marriage has become widely accepted (77% of Americans aged 38-43 have cohabited), which pushes marriage later and makes it less common. He also links cohabitation to higher divorce risk and less family stability for children. He calls for teaching the 'success sequence' alongside warnings about cohabitation's risks.

insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Less stable unions mean more household splits, which raises demand for separate housing and lowers household wealth.
